The key is sent as x-api-key, and anthropic-version: 2023-06-01 is added for you. The model list arrives with each model\'s limits and how it thinks: adaptively, with the level in output_config.effort, from Claude 4.6 on; with a token budget before that.

The key is sent as Authorization: Bearer. The answer limit goes in max_completion_tokens: reasoning models refuse max_tokens. The pro and codex families answer only on /responses, which needs an adapter of its own, so they are marked in the list.

The model list arrives with the limits: a context window for every model, an answer limit for nearly all, reasoning levels for about half; the rest use their default level. The list is public, so the key is checked on its own, on /key.

Kiro has no public API: underneath it is Amazon Q Developer, reached the way Kiro Account Manager reaches it. A Google or GitHub sign-in needs only its refreshToken; a Builder ID one also its clientId and clientSecret, pasted as JSON or as the manager exports an account. The token is exchanged for an access token, the models come from ListAvailableModels, and replies arrive as an AWS event stream. An exchange can hand out a new refresh token, which signs out a Kiro IDE holding the old one, and the other way round. AWS does not endorse this use.

Base URL up to /v1; the app adds the route. Every server has /chat/completions; /messages is on Ollama from 0.14 and LM Studio, usually not on vLLM or llama.cpp. A local server rarely needs a key, and plain http is fine on your own network.
